# Workshop Simulation — Audience Questions

*Generated by running the full slide deck and speaker notes as a simulated audience.
Audience profile: tech-heavy (engineers, architects, data scientists) plus some business/compliance.
Organised by the point in the workshop where the question would arise.*

---

## Round 1 — Sections 01–08 (Opening through Engine Depth)

### Q1.1 — Data quality / dedup hash
**"You showed the dedup hash collapsing 8 records to 4 before any data hits Senzing. But if you collapse KYC-001 and WIRE-A12 to the same hash and de-duplicate them, aren't you throwing away the fact that they came from two different source systems? Senzing can weight sources differently — so sending both records instead of one would give Senzing better signal, not less."**

*Raised after: Section 03 — The Best ER Is the One You Don't Need*

---

### Q1.2 — Normalise don't replace, GDPR tension
**"You said 'disk is cheap, lost signal is permanent' and that you keep original records. But we have GDPR right-to-erasure obligations. When a data subject asks to be forgotten, how do you reconcile that with never deleting records? Does the architecture have a clean answer, or is this a legal exception carved out separately?"**

*Raised after: Section 03*

---

### Q1.3 — Phase 1 vs. Phase 2 resolution boundary
**"I'm not clear on where the line is between 'structural fact' and 'resolution decision'. You showed two records sharing the same passport node in Phase 1 as a structural fact — but isn't that already implying they're the same person? What stops an analyst querying Phase 1 data from drawing that conclusion and acting on it?"**

*Raised after: Section 05 — Phase 1, Data In*

---

### Q1.4 — Input graph vs. resolved graph: one database or two?
**"You mention a 'graph input layer' and a 'resolved graph layer' — are these two separate Neo4j instances, two separate databases inside one instance, different labels within the same graph? The architecture diagram has two different boxes. What's the physical separation?"**

*Raised after: Section 04 — Architecture*

---

### Q1.5 — Senzing configuration: who does it?
**"You said Senzing is configurable — data sources, entity types, scoring rules. But who actually does the configuration? Is there a default financial crime config we start from, or do we need to bring in Senzing professional services? And how often does it need retuning once deployed?"**

*Raised after: Section 06 — Senzing Fundamentals*

---

### Q1.6 — Candidate retrieval at scale
**"You said Senzing doesn't score every new record against every existing record — it retrieves a small candidate set first. How does it build that candidate set? Is it a standard inverted index, or something more sophisticated? And what's the false-negative rate for candidate retrieval — i.e., how often does the engine miss a match because the right candidate never made the shortlist?"**

*Raised after: Section 06 — Senzing Fundamentals*

---

### Q1.7 — MATCH_LEVEL_CODE semantics
**"You showed RESOLVED, RETIRED, and POSSIBLY_RELATED as match-level codes. What's the operational difference between POSSIBLY_RELATED and POSSIBLE_MATCH? Do you create an EntityGroup for POSSIBLY_RELATED, or does it sit in a separate bucket that analysts review?"**

*Raised after: Section 07 — From Graph Records to Senzing*

---

### Q1.8 — The no-fusion rule and query performance
**"You said you never fuse record properties into the EntityGroup, and aggregation happens at query time RBAC-filtered. So for every analyst query, you're running a multi-hop graph traversal across potentially hundreds of records. What does that do to query latency in a large deployment? Have you benchmarked it?"**

*Raised after: Section 07 — From Graph Records to Senzing*

---

### Q1.9 — Multi-script matching: do we really send all 13 aliases?
**"The Kerimova record with 13 names across 4 scripts is impressive. But do we send all 13 aliases in the NAMES array to Senzing, or does Senzing pick them up from the OFAC source itself? And if we're integrating our own KYC system that only has Latin text, does the cross-script matching still help us at all?"**

*Raised after: Section 08 — Engine Depth*

---

### Q1.10 — Build vs. buy: open-source alternatives
**"You made a strong build-vs-buy case for Senzing. But there are open-source ER frameworks — Dedupe.io, Splink, even LLM-based approaches. Why specifically Senzing vs. those, for an operational production context?"**

*Raised after: Section 08 — Engine Depth*

---

## Round 2 — Phases 3–6 (Living Architecture through Consumption)

### Q2.1 — Senzing engine version upgrades
**"If Senzing is deterministic given a fixed engine version and configuration — what happens when you upgrade the engine? Does every entity get re-resolved? That could be a massive operational event with thousands of split and merge cascades. How do you manage that?"**

*Raised after: Phase 3 — Living Architecture*

---

### Q2.2 — Record update semantics
**"You said 'update = new versioned record, not mutation'. So if KYC-001 gets a corrected passport number, I land a new record version and push it to Senzing. But doesn't that mean Senzing now sees two records — the old version and the new version — both attributed to KYC-001? How does Senzing know the old payload is superseded?"**

*Raised after: Phase 3*

---

### Q2.3 — Redo storms: quantification
**"You mentioned redo storms as a real operational concern. Can you give us ballpark numbers? In a dataset of 1 million records, what does a 'bad' redo cascade look like — 100 affected entities? 10,000? And how long does Senzing take to work through it?"**

*Raised after: Phase 3 / Phase 4*

---

### Q2.4 — Split: downstream entity ID hell
**"When an EntityGroup splits, the downstream systems that were tracking entity_id 1001 now need to know it split into 1001 and 1042. If you have 15 downstream consumers — alerting systems, sanctions screening, BI dashboards — how do you propagate that split notification? Is there a change-data-capture mechanism for EntityGroup lifecycle events?"**

*Raised after: Phase 3*

---

### Q2.5 — Explainability for splits
**"You showed that the WHY payload on RESOLVED_TO edges explains merges. But for a split — when a record is removed from an EntityGroup — what does the WHY look like? Is it 'the record that contradicted the prior grouping' or is it the per-feature scores from the new grouping?"**

*Raised after: Phase 4 — Explainability*

---

### Q2.6 — Observability: graph queries are the dashboards
**"You said all observability is graph queries — redo rates, affected entity counts, stability. But graph queries run on the same database that's doing live ingestion. At high ingest volumes, won't your dashboards compete with production traffic? What's the performance isolation story?"**

*Raised after: Phase 4 — Observability*

---

### Q2.7 — Trust IDs and record immutability tension
**"In Phase 1, records are immutable — if the source updates, that's a new versioned record. But in Phase 5, the graph decision layer writes a TRUST_ID onto an existing record. That's a mutation of a record to inject derived data. Doesn't that break the immutability principle? And if the trust ID was written by the graph, does Senzing 'know' it's derived signal vs. source signal?"**

*Raised after: Phase 5 — Trust IDs*

---

### Q2.8 — Trust ID: force-apart persistence
**"If I set different trust IDs on two records to force them apart, what happens when a brand new record arrives with a strong feature match to both? Does Senzing respect the existing force-apart and still keep them separate? Or does the new high-specificity feature overrule the trust ID?"**

*Raised after: Phase 5*

---

### Q2.9 — RBAC and compliance lens
**"You said candidate generation for trust IDs runs under a 'compliance lens' — elevated access across sources. That's a powerful position in the system. Who controls what runs under the compliance lens? If that component is compromised or misconfigured, it can read every record across every source. What's the security model?"**

*Raised after: Phase 5 — Overrides and Access Control*

---

### Q2.10 — Trust ID loops: cycle depth cap
**"You said you cap cycle depth as a safety net for trust-ID loops. What does that cap look like in practice? Is it a hard integer limit? And what happens when you hit the cap — do you raise an alert, retry later, or stop silently?"**

*Raised after: Phase 5*

---

### Q2.11 — Face embeddings in regulated environments
**"You mentioned face embedding vectors for trust-ID positive signals. Using biometric data for identity resolution in regulated financial environments has explicit GDPR article requirements — explicit consent, biometric data processing agreements, etc. Is that architecture pattern actually deployable in EU financial institutions, or is it a flag risk?"**

*Raised after: Phase 5 — Risks*

---

### Q2.12 — Smart ER and non-Hume consumers
**"The Hume 3.0 demo looks useful. But not everyone in this room uses Hume. If I want to build the same entity-aware expand in my own application using the Neo4j graph you described, is there a standard query pattern? Or is the Smart ER traversal logic proprietary to Hume?"**

*Raised after: Phase 6 — Hume 3.0*

---

## Round 3 — Cross-cutting follow-up after close

### Q3.1 — Where does Senzing live in the infrastructure?
**"Throughout the workshop you talked about 'pushing records to Senzing' and 'getting affected entities back'. But what is Senzing physically — is it a SaaS API, an on-premises service, a library we embed? Can we run it air-gapped?"**

*General question at end*

---

### Q3.2 — Cost model at scale
**"This architecture has Senzing, a Neo4j graph (possibly two layers), a decision layer, potentially Hume. What does the infrastructure cost model look like at 10 million entities? Is the dominant cost Senzing licensing, Neo4j Enterprise, or compute?"**

*Business audience question*

---

### Q3.3 — Cold start: migration from existing ER system
**"We already have an entity resolution system — old, batch, no graph. How do we migrate to this architecture? Do we backfill everything through Senzing and build the graph from scratch, or is there a migration path that respects existing entity IDs?"**

*Practical concern*

---

### Q3.4 — The 'Senzing is the source of truth' rule under force-merge
**"You stated as a rule: 'Senzing is the source of truth for resolution'. But when an analyst does a force-merge in Hume, Senzing re-resolves and produces the merge. Who actually made the decision — the analyst or Senzing? If Senzing's re-resolution with the trust ID doesn't produce the merge the analyst wanted, what happens?"**

*Conceptual tension*

---

### Q3.5 — Possibly-related: false positive cost
**"You briefly mentioned POSSIBLY_RELATED as an output level. In AML screening, a false negative (missing a real connection) is far worse than a false positive (surfacing a spurious connection). How does the architecture handle the POSSIBLY_RELATED bucket — is it a manual review queue, or does it feed back into the loop?"**

*Compliance audience question*

---

### Q3.6 — What happens to EntityGroup if Senzing is unavailable?
**"What happens to the pipeline when Senzing goes down? Do incoming records queue in the graph input layer and catch up when Senzing recovers? Or does the whole pipeline stall? And when Senzing comes back, does the catch-up replay produce the right EntityGroup state?"**

*Operational resilience*

---

### Q3.7 — Senzing vs. graph for person vs. organisation ER
**"Is the same Senzing configuration used for both person and organisation resolution, or do you run separate Senzing instances with separate configs? Organisation ER has very different signal patterns — company suffixes, registry IDs, ownership chains — vs. person ER."**

*Technical / configuration depth*

---

## Round 4 — Follow-up after hearing the answers (sharp audience, post-break)

### Q4.1 — Shared passport node survives a Senzing force-apart
**"In your Phase 1, two records share the same :Passport node because the raw data has the same passport number. Then Senzing resolves them as separate entities — maybe via a force-apart trust ID, or just by scoring. The shared :Passport node is still there in the graph, silently implying a connection. Do you remove it? Or does it become a liability in future investigations where an analyst sees it and thinks it means something?"**

*Follow-up after: A1.3 (structural fact vs. resolution decision)*

---

### Q4.2 — Decision layer trigger for POSSIBLY_RELATED pairs
**"You said POSSIBLY_RELATED pairs feed into the Phase 5 decision layer as candidates. But with millions of records, there could be tens of thousands of POSSIBLY_RELATED pairs. Does the decision layer continuously scan all of them? Or does something specific trigger evaluation of a pair? If it's event-triggered, what's the event — a new POSSIBLY_RELATED appearing, or something else?"**

*Follow-up after: A1.7 and A3.5*

---

### Q4.3 — Trust ID re-ingest overwrite risk
**"You said the trust ID sits on the graph-side record representation, not the source payload. But what happens when the KYC source re-ingests KYC-001 with a new version? The graph lands a new record node — but does it copy the trust ID from the previous version onto the new node? Or does the trust ID silently get lost, and Senzing re-resolves without it?"**

*Follow-up after: A2.2 and A2.7*

---

### Q4.4 — Trust ID vs. future contradicting evidence
**"If an analyst force-merges two entities via trust ID, and six months later a new record arrives with strong evidence they are different people — a corrected national ID, a registry correction — does Senzing still honour the trust ID and keep them merged? Or does the new evidence override the trust ID? Who wins?"**

*Follow-up after: A2.8 and A3.4*

---

### Q4.5 — Entity ID instability as a permanent coordination problem
**"You said downstream consumers need to handle entity ID transitions (splits, merges) by tracking a transition table. But in a living system, these transitions happen continuously. Are you saying every consumer has to permanently subscribe to entity lifecycle events and maintain their own mapping, forever? What's the practical ceiling — at what entity ID churn rate does this become unmanageable?"**

*Follow-up after: A2.4*

---

### Q4.6 — Configuration tuning loop: does the decision layer inform Senzing config?
**"In Phase 5, the trust-ID log shows the graph correcting the engine repeatedly for the same type of error — say, always force-merging certain name transliterations. At what point is that a signal to retune Senzing's scoring config, rather than continuously overriding it with trust IDs? Does the architecture surface that signal, or is it something you have to spot manually?"**

*Follow-up after: Phase 5 overall — TODOS.md §11 mentions this as an open question*

---

### Q4.7 — Hume vs. build-your-own consumer
**"The whole Phase 6 is shown through Hume. You said non-Hume consumers can write the Cypher themselves. But the RBAC logic, the WHY surfacing, the entity-aware search — is all of that documented in a way that a team can build against the graph directly, without a Hume dependency? Or is Hume the only supported path to get entity-aware navigation with proper access control?"**

*Follow-up after: A2.12 and Phase 6*

---

### Q4.8 — The 'four properties' checklist: who audits it?
**"You presented four properties — near real-time, idempotent, observable, explainable — as the checklist for a properly operationalised ER system. In a running production system, who audits that these four are actually holding? An EntityGroup that's been silently unstable for three months without anyone noticing is not 'observable' in practice, even if the observability tooling exists."**

*Closing meta-question — valid at any point in the workshop*
